newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian cotton drops on poor demand, higher supply.
newsitem.headline: Indian cotton drops on poor demand, higher supply.

text.p: Cotton prices dropped on Thursday on sluggish demand from mills and a slowdown in cotton purchases by state-owned agencies, traders said.
"Higher new crop arrivals triggered selling in the market," said a trader. "Mills kept to the sidelines expecting a further fall in prices."
He said the Cotton Corporation of India, the country's main cotton purchasing agency, had also reduced its market buying.
In spot, Bengal-deshi dropped 20 rupees to 750/800 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) and Punjab saw-ginned rose 5.0/10 rupees to 1,375/1,600 rupees per maund.
Gujarat cotton held steady in a narrow price band.
Gujarat Kalyan (medium staple) was quiet at 11,000/11,300 rupees per candy (355.56 kg) and Sankar-4 (long staple) was steady at 16,000/18,000 rupees per candy.
